standard_prerequisites.name: Surjectivity of spectra for integral and for radical extensions
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma algebra-lemma-integral-overring-surjective (00GQ, proof lines 625-626) and Lemma algebra-lemma-surjective-spec-radical-ideal (00FI, proof lines 627-628)
standard_prerequisites.use: Supply that Spec(R') -> Spec(R) and Spec(A') -> Spec(A) are surjective, which is what produces the prime q' of A' lying over (0) of A.

core_obligations: Reduce to a discrete valuation ring: choose a minimal prime q of R, note R/q is one-dimensional and not a field, and choose a discrete valuation ring A dominating R/q with the same fraction field; let v be its valuation, and observe that a and b become nonzero elements of A with v(a) > 0 because a lies in the maximal ideal (proof lines 613-620).

Propagate the datum to a finite extension: for a finite ring extension R contained in R' set A' = A tensor_R R', which has Spec(A') -> Spec(A) surjective because Spec(R') -> Spec(R) is, pick a prime q' of A' over (0) of A and set A'' = A'/q', so that A contained in A'' is a finite extension of rings (proof lines 623-631).

Estimate the valuation: choose a maximal ideal m'' of A'' over the maximal ideal of A and a discrete valuation ring A''' dominating A''_{m''}; then A -> A''' is an extension of discrete valuation rings, the relation b = a^m c holds in A''', hence v'''(b) >= m v'''(a), and since v''' = e v with e the ramification index one gets m <= n for n = v(b)/v(a) (proof lines 632-638).
proof_roadmap: Choose a discrete valuation ring A dominating R/q with the same fraction field and compute v(a) > 0, so that n = v(b)/v(a) is defined (proof lines 613-621).

For a given finite extension R contained in R', propagate the picture to A' = A tensor_R R', cut by a prime over (0) and pass to a discrete valuation ring A''' dominating a localisation of the residue ring, so that the divisibility relation b = a^m c survives (proof lines 623-635).
Compare the two valuations in A''': v'''(b) >= m v'''(a) and v''' = e v give m <= n, so n is a uniform bound over all finite extensions (proof lines 636-638).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that in a one-dimensional Noetherian local ring with nonzerodivisors a, b and a in the maximal ideal, the exponent m such that b = a^m c can be realised inside a finite ring extension is bounded independently of the extension (statement lines 606-609). The proof produces the bound by leaving the ring: a discrete valuation ring A dominating a minimal quotient R/q records v(a) > 0, and the bound n = v(b)/v(a) is then shown to hold for every finite extension R contained in R' by propagating the picture along A tensor_R R', cutting down by a prime over (0) and comparing valuations in a further discrete valuation ring A''' dominating a localisation, where the relation b = a^m c forces v'''(b) >= m v'''(a) and v''' = e v (proof lines 613-638). The non-formal content is this chain of base changes preserving the divisibility relation while keeping control of the ramification. The claim is H2.
